(cannot be checked against operative state)' and 'still emits nothing... even when operativeState is null (nothing to check either way)' tests) - it is an intentional, already-known design decision, not an undiscovered defect. task5_blocker5RealDefect.reclassificationReverification: Read tools.ts in full (605 lines), independently re-derived every one of the 14 tools' own real runtime behavior (not the classification table alone). getContextBundleComponent and getSharedCapContext genuinely use summarizeItemWithSupersession, which calls the real getNodeSupersessionStatus against the SAME supersessionIndex buildToolSet builds once per attempt, keyed by item.structuralNodeId, failing closed to UNKNOWN for a structuralNodeId-less item (e.g. a DEFINITION/DEFINITION_DEPENDENCY context item) - confirmed correct, matches doc 04's own claim exactly.

newDefectFound.rootCause: getDefinition's own execute() body checks `if (operative?.currentText) { ...return 'amended'... }` and, if that is falsy, unconditionally falls through to RAW base-document text via getScopedDefinitionFullText, labeled only `source: 'base-document'`. Its SECTION-kind sibling getOperativeProvision, by contrast, discloses `status: view.status` in BOTH its 'found' branch AND its 'not found, raw fallback' branch - it NEVER silently drops the real OperativeProvisionView's own status. getDefinition discloses NOTHING about `operative.status` in EITHER branch. Per operative-state.ts's own real, independently-confirmed rule (`currentText = null` is set whenever targetResolutionStatus !== 'UNIQUE', i.e. for a real AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION amendment - exactly BLOCKER-6's own scenario shape), a term with a REAL, ON-FILE, KNOWN amendment record whose target could not be uniquely resolved reaches getDefinition's `operative?.currentText` check as falsy and falls through to the SAME raw/stale text and the SAME 'source: base-document' label a term that was NEVER amended at all would also receive - there is no way for the calling LLM (or a human reading the tool_result JSON) to tell these two cases apart.
newDefectFound.whyWorkstreamBMissedIt: doc 04's own per-tool table records 'getDefinition: findProvisionView-first, correct as claimed' - this checked only the HAPPY branch (operative.currentText truthy) and never independently constructed the falsy-currentText/real-ambiguity case to check what the OTHER branch discloses.
newDefectFound.reproduction: Constructed a real AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION OperativeProvisionView (targetResolutionStatus: 'AMBIGUOUS', status: 'OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL', currentText: null, candidateSourceNodeIds populated, reviewRequired: true, unresolvedIssues populated - directly modeled on cross-module-propagation-chains.test.ts's own real 'Chain 2' BLOCKER-6 construction) for a term 'Permitted Investments' whose real base-document text says $8,000,000. Called the real buildToolSet's getDefinition.execute({ term: 'Permitted Investments' }). OBSERVED: `{ term: 'Permitted Investments', source: 'base-document', text: '...$8,000,000...', truncated: false }` - no `status`, no `unresolvedIssues`, and the full JSON response contains no occurrence of 'AMBIGUOUS'/'PARTIAL'/'review' (case-insensitive) anywhere. CONTRAST CONTROL: the identical scenario built as a SECTION-kind provision and queried via getOperativeProvision correctly discloses `status: 'OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL'` and the honest placeholder `currentText: '(no current text recorded)'` - proving this is a genuine asymmetry in getDefinition specifically, not a property of OperativeProvisionView.currentText being null in general. CROSS-CHECK: getRelatedAmendments (a DIFFERENT tool) correctly discloses the same real PARTIAL status for the identical term when called directly - confirming the operative-state record itself is fully correct, on file, and available; only getDefinition's own fallback branch fails to consult it, and the LLM is under no obligation to call getRelatedAmendments before trusting getDefinition's own description ('use this... when the meaning... was not already included in your initial context').
newDefectFound.liveWiring: buildToolSet is called by lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/caller.ts (the REAL semantic compiler the live orchestrator uses via getSemanticCaller/compilePackageToIR - independently confirmed by grep) - this is a live, exploitable, in-production tool-calling surface, not a theoretical or disabled code path.
newDefectFound.severity: A material covenant basket definition subject to a real, on-file, unresolved amendment ambiguity can be served to the compiling LLM as plain, uncontested fact, with the SAME label a genuinely never-amended term would carry. Any rule the compiler builds depending on that definition can reach a clean COMPLETE/VERIFIED outcome with zero indication anywhere in the compilation record that the underlying term's own meaning is contested.

finalDispositions.BLOCKER-6_rationale: cross-reference-audit.ts's own charter mechanism (candidateSourceNodeIds-based matching for AMBIGUOUS DEFINITION-kind provisions) is independently re-verified correct under a fresh 3-way/cross-term-isolation attack. However, this same recertification found that the exact harm BLOCKER-6 exists to prevent (an ambiguous DEFINITION amendment reaching a falsely-confident downstream conclusion) is independently, concretely reproducible today through a DIFFERENT, coupled, unguarded pathway (BLOCKER-5's own getDefinition tool, in the live semantic-compiler tool-calling surface) that BLOCKER-6's own remediation scope never covered.
